gaps: layout-narrow: the narrow-viewport label check is broken and matches any port. measure() decides prevWordVisible from Range.getBoundingClientRect() on the Previous text node. That returns the text's layout box even when the span is visually hidden by max-sm:sr-only (clip plus a 1px box). So the original itself records layout.w600.prevWordVisible=true and layout.w340.prevWordVisible=true, although its prevWidth is 36 (chevron only). A port that keeps 'Previous'/'Next' visible below 640px would match on every compared key: rowWiderThanCard is false at 600 and true at 340 either way, and chevronsOutsideCard is true either way. Fix: (1) Decide visibility from the text's parent element instead: getBoundingClientRect() width and height > 4, and computed clip/clip-path not rect(0px, 0px, 0px, 0px) / inset(50%), or use checkVisibility() on a box that is not clipped. Then check that the original gives true at 1100 and false at 600 and 340. (2) Also compare the Previous and Next control widths at w600 and w340 as kind px (layout.w600.prevWidth, layout.w340.prevWidth, plus nextWidth). At those sizes they are a fixed 36px square that does not depend on text width. Keep the 1100px width as info.

contract v2 (no nesting selectors) / underline-spring, reduced-motion, current-page-noop, accessible-names (p2-vue-3): window.__ul only looks for the underline among descendants of the [aria-current=page] control, so it assumes the bar is nested inside the button or link. A correct port that renders the bar as a sibling inside the same list item finds no underline. Every spring and reduced curve then throws, and a11y.underlineTabindex reads [[],[],[]]. This produces false failures, not false passes, but it breaks the contract rule. Fix: look for the aria-hidden, non-svg, thin (height <= 6) element anywhere in the nav whose horizontal centre lies within the current control's column, for example inside the current control's closest role=listitem, instead of only among its descendants.

gaps: hover-lift-and-tooltip / overflow-lift-and-tooltip / focus-lift-and-tooltip (the 520/34 spring): overshoot is never compared. emitCurve stores it only as overshootsInfo (info), min/max are px with a 1.5px tolerance on a 3px travel, and settleMs uses a 0.5px band, so an overshoot up to about 0.45px is invisible to it. t50/t90 move by less than 25 percent between damping 34 and about 25, so a visibly bouncier spring (overshoot 0.3 to 0.45px against the original 0.088px) passes every check. Fix: add `${prefix}.overshoot` as kind ratio, computed as the excursion past `end` in the travel direction divided by |end-start| (original about 0.03). Also tighten settleMs to a 0.1px band, or add `${prefix}.settle01Ms`. While doing that, fix the overshootsInfo sign test: `prefix.endsWith(".in")` is false for `.in2`, so in2 currently reports 3 instead of -0.088. Use the sign of (end-start) instead.

hover-lift-and-tooltip (the tooltip "appears instantly", no entrance): only opacity is compared (tipInstant = opacity >= 0.99 within 100ms). tipScaleAtAppear is info, and the tooltip position is read once, 150ms after the sample window. A port whose tooltip scales in (0.9 to 1) or slides up a few px over 100 to 200ms at full opacity therefore passes. Fix: make tipScaleAtAppear compared (exact boolean >= 0.97, or ratio). In __sample, also record each frame's tooltip bottom relative to the disc top while a tooltip is visible, and emit `${prefix}.tipTravel` (px, max minus min across frames) as a compared check. The same applies to the overflow and reduced-motion hoverFlow calls, which share emitCurve.

Robustness, contract rule 'same script must fit all implementations' (affects hover/focus/overflow-lift-and-tooltip, tooltip-hidden-from-at, reduced-motion and the p3-svelte-7 combo keys): __tipEls counts a tooltip as present whenever checkVisibility({checkVisibilityCSS:true}) passes, and that ignores opacity. It also skips any tooltip placed inside the role=img element. A correct port that keeps every tooltip mounted and hides it with opacity 0, or nests the aria-hidden tooltip inside the img span, gets wrong tipCount, combo.*.tips and tipGoneWithin100ms results (a false fail, not a false pass), so the rerun cannot tell a real failure from a harness artefact. Fix: filter leaves by effective opacity > 0.01 (or checkVisibility({opacityProperty:true})). Exclude only text inside the img's own accessible content (for example, skip leaves under the img unless they are inside an aria-hidden subtree that is not the initials span), or find the tooltip as the aria-hidden visible text nearest above the active disc, as __tipBox does.

underline-spring / reduced-motion (root cause, pagination.mjs line 48-58 `__ul`): the underline is only found when its horizontal centre lies inside the current cell's column (+-0.5px). Framer draws the bar inside the NEW cell with a transform, so in its offset frames (-20px forward, +40px backward, -136px on 7 to 12) the centre is outside the column and the bar is dropped (u=null), and `curve()` skips those frames. The baseline shows this: forward start -15.38 and backward start +14.34, where the checklist and the judges measured -20 and +40; reduced.card1.6to7 shows 0 moving frames, where the checklist says one frame at -20. Fix: during sampling, find the bar without the column filter: the aria-hidden, non-svg element in the nav with height <= 6 and width > 4 (ellipses are 36px tall and drop out), or the element picked at rest and followed while it stays connected. Keep the column rule only for the static first-render inset checks. Then rerun the three original baselines and confirm start is about -20 (a), +40 (b), +44 (prev5to4), -24 (next4to5) and that reduced.card1.6to7.offsetFrame is true with start about -20.

p3-svelte-10: not caught. The original baseline has reduced.card1.6to7.offsetFrame=false, start=0, peak=0, movingFrames=0 (the single offset frame is filtered out, see `__ul` above). A Svelte port with no offset frame gives the same values and passes every named check. After the `__ul` fix, the original must read offsetFrame=true and start/peak about -20, or the defect cannot fail.

underline-spring checklist (a) vs (b), 'backward is larger and slightly slower than forward': cannot be told apart. Because of the clipping, start/peak read about 15px both ways (-15.38 and +14.34). A port with a symmetric +20px backward offset would first be seen at about +15 (inside the 1.5px band), settle in about 265ms against 299 (inside 25%), and t50 98ms against 133 (inside the 40ms floor). It passes. The `__ul` fix restores real amplitudes. Also add a compared check on the asymmetry itself, for example spring.ab.backwardLarger (exact: |b.start| > 1.5*|a.start|).

contract v2 selectors (lines 60-62, 64, 672-677, 598, 619): rows, ellipses and controls are found by tag and nesting: `querySelectorAll("li")`, `li.querySelector("a, button, [aria-disabled]")`, and live.tag compared exact to "li". A port that builds the list from role=list/listitem, or controls from role=button/link, gets empty rows and fails for no real reason. Use `li, [role=listitem]` and `a, button, [role=button], [role=link], [aria-disabled]`, and compare the live region's role (listitem) instead of the tag name.

locale (lines 631-659): the locale contexts skip settle(), the pointer press and the wait for rest that the contract requires on every target, so any original autoplay can move the page before locale.*.currentName is read. These contexts also do not register the console and pageerror listeners. Call the same settle(page) after waitFor, and attach the console handlers.

tab-order / p3-vue-7 (keys tab.success.pay.order, tab.success.subscribe.order): tabWalk() does not start before the root when a button has focus. blur() plus a selection range does not move Chrome's focus-navigation starting point off the clicked button. The original's own baseline shows this: tab.success.pay.order = ["button:Apply code"] and tab.success.subscribe.order = ["button:Paid","button:Apply code"], when the full walk should be input > Subscribe > Paid > Apply code. The path defect is still caught today, but only because the walk happens to start right after the clicked button. The checks never confirm that the success-state button is itself a Tab stop or that the input and Subscribe come first, and the result depends on where each port leaves focus after a click (the p2 Vue run gives the same values as the original). Fix: give the walk a fixed start. Either insert a temporary tabindex=0 sentinel just before the root, focus it, then Tab; or focus the email textbox with getByRole and record it as the first stop. Then regenerate the baseline and check it reads [input, Subscribe, Paid, Apply code] for Pay and [input, Subscribed, Paid, Apply code] for Subscribe.

contract v2 locale (affects every item): the script hard-codes English demo copy to detect state and to wait for rest: IDLE (Subscribe / Pay $68.00 / Apply code), the derive() labels Subscribed / Paid / Code expired, the textbox name 'Email for restock news' and /fails on purpose/. With l=ja the original demo switches to Japanese (useDemoText), so open() throws 'demo never came to rest' in every scenario and the original's output has no checks at all. The port demos keep English (no locale in the LoadingButtonDemo ports), so tabOrder labels differ as well. Fix: make state detection independent of labels (aria-busy and live-region transitions, with idle and result labels read from each run's own first snapshot or result frame, and tab labels reduced to role only outside en). Or, since the component owns no visible string, have the script write one errors entry and skip when LOCALE !== 'en', and document that this block is checked in en only.

shrink-loading / success-subscribe / error-state (spring stiffness 240, damping 30): the width curves (subscribe.shrink, apply.shrink, subscribe.expand, apply.expand, subscribe.reset, apply.reset) only emit firstDir, animates, monotonic, reversalPx, end/min, overshoot and settleMs. A linear or ease-in-out width tween of about 430ms passes every one of them, so the spring easing the checklist requires is never verified. Fix: in widthSeg, add <name>.t50Ms and <name>.t90Ms (kind ms: time from the trigger until the width has covered 50% and 90% of start to end) and emit them in emitWidth for all six segments. Consider the same for press.idle (time to 50% of the 1 to 0.97 change).

label-crossfade (contract v2, static offsets): xfade.*.in.dxFromCenterMax is compared as px, but it is the horizontal offset of text inside its box. The original's xfade.subscribe.toSuccess value of 2.77px comes from Framer's layout scale correction while the button grows. A correct port that keeps the content centred reads about 0 and fails the 1.27..4.27 window. Fix: record it as info, or compare a boolean such as dxFromCenterMax < 4.

shrink-loading (minor): the spinner's shape from the checklist (a full ring at 25% opacity plus a solid quarter arc) is not measured. A port with a plain single arc or a full solid ring passes spinnerCount, spinnerSize and spinnerRotates. Fix: inside the spinner svg, add a compared count of stroked shapes and an exact boolean for whether one of them has a computed stroke-opacity or opacity of about 0.25 (an opacity, not a colour).

gaps: review-tooltip-entrance (also hover-lift-and-tooltip 'appears instantly'): window.__sample reads opacity, width and bottom from the tooltip container c = te[0][0], which is the closest [aria-hidden="true"] ancestor of the text leaves. If a port puts aria-hidden on a static outer wrapper and animates an inner element (for example a Vue <Transition> or Svelte transition:scale/fly inside <span aria-hidden>), a child's scale or translate does not change c's getBoundingClientRect, and a child's opacity is not in effOpacity(c), which only walks upward from c. So tipScaleAtAppear, tipTravel, tipFullMs and tipInstant all read 1, 0 and instant, and the entrance passes. Fix: in __sample, take op = min over the leaves of effOpacity(leaf) (leaf up to the document) and take w and tbot from the union of the leaves' rects, which do include ancestor transforms. Do the same in the rm.hover and overflow runs, since they share the helper.

hover-lift-and-tooltip / overflow-lift-and-tooltip / review-tooltip-entrance: short fades pass. hoverFlow.*.in.tipOpacityAtAppear is info, and tipInstant and tipAppearsWithin100ms only require full opacity within 100 ms, so a 60 to 90 ms opacity fade-in passes. On leave, tipGoneWithin100ms lets a fade-out of up to about 85 ms pass (the original is gone on the first frame, about 16 ms). That breaks the checklist's 'appears instantly' and 'disappears at once with no exit animation'. Fix: add phase-tolerant compared booleans from the frames, using the leaf-based opacity: <prefix>.in.tipPartialFrames = any post-trigger frame with tips>0 and 0.01<op<0.99 (exact; false in the original), and the same for .out and .ontoTip. Or compare tipOpacityAtAppear as ratio.

hover-lift-and-tooltip (spring 520/34): an ease-out tween can pass for the spring. The original overshoots by only 0.088 px (overshoot ratio 0.029), and the ratio tolerance is 0.03, so a port with no overshoot at all (a 150 to 200 ms ease-out tween, or an overdamped spring) gets 0 and falls inside 0..0.059. Its t50, t90, settleMs and settle01Ms also fall inside the 40 ms ms tolerance. Fix: add an exact boolean <prefix>.overshoots = (overshoot past end in px) > 0.03 for hoverFlow.leo.in/out/in2/out2, focus.leo.*, and overflow.*.in/out (true in the original, stable at 0.088 to 0.089 px across runs). review-bouncy-spring stays covered by the existing ratio.

overflow-lift-and-tooltip and focus-lift-and-tooltip: the lift on keyboard focus is measured only for Mina, Leo and Ava in the main stack. The overflow discs (+1.3K, +410, +94) and the related-row avatars are lifted only by hover. The tab walk records tooltips per stop but not position, so a port whose overflow disc (often a separate branch or component) shows the tooltip on focus but never lifts passes. Fix: in the tab-order scenario, record each stop's y relative to its rest top after it settles (wait about 400 ms, or poll until stable), rounded to an integer, as an exact array tab.focusLift (expected -3 on every img stop and 0 on the button). Also record the lift of the previous stop, to check it returned to 0.

Opacity is the max over the leaves of effOpacity(leaf) walked up to the document. The width and bottom come from the union of the leaf rects. I used max, not the min you suggested, because line 2 of the tooltip is dimmed on purpose (op2), so min would stay below 0.99 in the original and tipPartialFrames would read true there. __tipVis uses the same helper. The rm.hover and overflow runs share __sample, so they are covered.

Gap 2, short fades: new exact check <prefix>.tipPartialFrames. It is true if any frame after the trigger has a tooltip present with 0.01 < op < 0.99. gaps: label-crossfade: the direction of the incoming slide is never compared. xfade.*.in.startDy is info, slideT50Ms/slideT90Ms only measure |dy - endDy|, and dyRange is emitted only under reduced motion. A port whose new label enters from 6px ABOVE (y:-6 instead of +6) passes. Fix: in emitFade, add `${name}.in.firstDir` (kind dir: direction of the first movement larger than 0.3px; the original gives up) or `${name}.in.startDyRel` = startDy - endDy (kind px, relative to the rest position, about +6). Do it for every xfade, including xfade.pay.toSuccess.

label-crossfade (easing): the checklist asks for ease-out, not ease-in-out, but the timing keys cannot tell them apart. The original's in.t50Ms is about 50 to 55 and t90 about 100 to 116. compare.mjs allows at least 40ms, and a 140ms ease-in-out fade lands near t50=70 and t90=111, so it passes. Fix: interpolate the crossing times between frames inside crossT (no frame rounding) and add a shape ratio such as `${name}.in.t50OverT90` (kind ratio, about 0.42 for the original, about 0.63 for ease-in-out). The same gap exists for the check draw in success-subscribe and success-sticky ('0.28s with ease-out'): subscribe/pay.check.t50Ms of about 116 against about 140 for ease-in-out or linear is inside the 40ms tolerance. Add `subscribe.check.t50OverT90` and `pay.check.t50OverT90` as ratio.

label-crossfade (coverage): only Pay's loading to success crossfade is measured. The checklist says 'any state change'. Nothing measures Pay idle to inline loading, Paid to loading (repeat press), or Subscribe/Apply loading to idle under the inline style. A port that keeps 'Pay $68.00' static and only inserts or fades in the spinner passes. Fix: in S3, add xfade.pay.toLoading. Measure the incoming spinner opacity t50/t90, check that two 'Pay $68.00' text parts overlap for at least 2 frames (count), and check that the outgoing text reaches minDy of about -6 (px) with out.animates (exact). Find the outgoing part as the 'Pay $68.00' part whose opacity falls.

tab-order: 'spinners and icons never take focus' is checked only at idle (S1) and while a success check is showing (S8). No Tab walk runs while a spinner is on screen, so a port whose spinner svg or motion element becomes focusable during loading passes (the Vue motion-v focus-listener cause behind p3-vue-7 applies to spinners too). Fix: in S8 (or a new step), click Pay, start tabWalk about 300ms later (loading lasts 1800ms) and emit `tab.loading.pay.order` (exact). Do the same for Subscribe in its 1400ms loading window (`tab.loading.subscribe.order`).

first-render: the mount probe records for 1000ms from document start, not from the moment the three buttons appear. On a port whose app mounts late (Vite dev first load, slow hydration), the probe sees only a few frames or none. With one frame, mountTravel is 0 and a slide-only entry animation passes first.noEntryAnimation and first.mountTravel. Fix: start the 1000ms window at the first frame where btns().length >= 3. Also emit `first.mountFrameCount` (count, or an exact boolean >= 20) so a short capture fails instead of passing.

contract v2 static offsets (label-crossfade): `${name}.in.centredWithin4px` (exact) is derived from the absolute horizontal offset of the content group from the button centre. The original already reads 2.77px on xfade.subscribe.toSuccess, close to the 4px threshold, so the baseline will flake and the key will be dropped as unstable. Fix: make it a relative measure (the change of that offset across the fade frames, as px) or keep it as info and rely on maxHeight plus a width-stacking check. Otherwise the side-by-side stacking it guards against loses its compared check.

contract coverage / locale: for l != en the script writes no checks and a single error with item 'all', which is not a checklist id. A locale run then passes trivially, and the coverage rule (each all/web item has a compared check or an errors entry saying why) is not met per item. Fix: write one errors entry per checklist id with the reason, or better, still run the locale-independent checks (widths, timings, aria-busy, focus, tab count, reduced motion) with the state labels read from the first render instead of the hard-coded English IDLE list.

verdicts.label: p2-svelte
defects: Lift spring starts with a stale velocity on every lift and drop after the first: every in/out/in2/out2/ontoTip curve for hover Leo, focus Mina/Leo/Ava and all three overflow discs has firstDir reversed (for example hoverFlow.leo.in up expected, down got), counterTravel about 0.39 to 0.41 (original 0), and settle01Ms about 271 to 284 against about 162 to 175. tipAT.ontoTip.firstDir up vs down comes from the same cause. Source: lift() calls controls?.stop() and then animate(node,{y},springs.snappy) with no velocity reset, so motion carries the previous velocity into the next spring.

Hover and focus share one state per stack: activeKey is a single $state ('only one tooltip at a time'), so hovering Leo C. while Noah W. has keyboard focus takes away Noah's lift and tooltip. combo.both.tips got only Leo (expected Leo and Noah), tipCount 1 vs 2, noahLift 0 vs -3; after the pointer leaves, afterLeave.tips is [] vs Noah, tipCount 0 vs 1, noahLift 0 vs -3, although focus stays on Noah. The original gives each Lift its own useState, so both stay active. The same thing fails under reduced motion (rm.combo.both/afterLeave tips and tipCount).

verdicts.label: p3-svelte
defects: Same stale-velocity spring as p2-svelte: liftY calls animate(node,{y},springs.snappy) after ctl.stop() without velocity 0. Every hover, focus and overflow in/out/in2/out2/ontoTip curve starts the wrong way (firstDir reversed, counterTravel about 0.39 to 0.41 vs 0) and settles in about 278 to 287ms against about 162 to 175. tipAT.ontoTip.firstDir up vs down comes from the same cause.

A single activeKey per stack ties hover and focus together: with Noah W. focused, hovering Leo C. drops Noah's tooltip and lift (combo.both.tips [Leo] vs [Leo, Noah], tipCount 1 vs 2, noahLift 0 vs -3; afterLeave tips [] vs [Noah], tipCount 0 vs 1, noahLift 0 vs -3). The original keeps separate state in each Lift. Also fails under reduced motion (rm.combo.*).

verdicts.label: p3-svelte-fixed
defects: The velocity fix ({...springs.snappy, velocity: 0}) clears every curve failure, but the single shared activeKey is still there. Hovering Leo C. while Noah W. keeps keyboard focus removes Noah's tooltip and lift: combo.both.tips [Leo C. / Osaka, 5 hours ago] vs both Leo and Noah, combo.both.tipCount 1 vs 2, combo.both.noahLift 0 vs -3. After the pointer leaves: combo.afterLeave.tips [] vs [Noah W. / Taichung, yesterday], tipCount 0 vs 1, noahLift 0 vs -3, with focus still on Noah. The reduced-motion run shows the same (rm.combo.both.tips/tipCount, rm.combo.afterLeave.tips/tipCount). Fix: give each lift box its own active flag (or a set of active keys) instead of one activeKey.
